## Hi, I'm Josh

I'm a Ph.D. student in the [Department of Statistical Science](https://stat.duke.edu) at Duke
University, working with Jerry Reiter and Fan Li.

My research sits where **causal inference** meets **missing data**. Most methods for asking
"did this treatment help, and for *whom*?" quietly assume you know who was treated. Often you
don't — an exposure that was never logged, a hazard recorded for only part of a population, a
survey nobody answered. I build Bayesian methods that estimate heterogeneous effects anyway,
and that carry the uncertainty about *who was treated* all the way through to the final
intervals.

Before Duke I graduated summa cum laude from UCLA in 2024 with a B.S. in Applied Mathematics,
Statistics and Data Science. Alongside my methods work I collaborate as a biostatistician with
Duke Radiology, UC San Diego's Moores Cancer Center, and previously Stanford Medicine — which
keeps me honest about what messy, real clinical data actually looks like.

I also care a great deal about teaching: in Summer 2026 I was instructor of record for
[STA 199: Introduction to Data Science and Statistical Thinking](https://sta199-su26-2.github.io/).

Outside the department you'll find me on the court with Duke Men's Club Volleyball, performing
with Duke Chinese Dance, flipping with Duke Gymnastics, or loudly defending UCLA sports deep in
ACC country.
